resolutions.what: Both prose descriptions now state 4 conjuncts and name the fourth (no eval case feeds the endpoint, or any `/api/` path on that host, to a run through its `input` block), with the PR #58 R2 red-first evidence cited beside the other three: the probe case's green `{'passed': True, ..., 'cases_scanned': 6}` on a rule-6 violation, then `{'ground_truth_endpoint_fed_to_the_executor': ['zz-tmp-leak-probe.json']}`. AND the count is derived, not re-typed: `docs-numbers-are-derived` gains `counts['gt_conjuncts'] = len(_check_ground_truth_endpoint_eval_only()['wrong'])`, one key per conjunct, quoted back out of ADR-030 §The ground-truth-endpoint boundary and support-matrix D30 through the `doc_quotes` block R1 added.
resolutions.red_first: two directions, both run. (1) Grader extended, prose still stale: {'doc_does_not_say': 'enforces\n4 conjuncts, each watched red before it was green', 'doc': 'specs/decisions/ADR-030-m41-sec10k-inspector-probe.md'} and {'doc_does_not_say': '`sec10k-ground-truth-endpoint-eval-only`, 4 conjuncts each watched red', 'doc': 'docs/support-matrix.md'} — the exact two sentences the reviewer named. (2) The direction that matters for recurrence: with the invariant stubbed to return five `wrong` keys, both documents redden at '5 conjuncts' without either being touched. A conjunct added in code now reddens the prose before the commit that adds it can go green.
resolutions.note: The count is `len(wrong)` because that is the shape the check already returns and a second registry would be one more thing to keep in sync. Two ceilings, both in the code comment and one of them in the ADR prose: `bool(cases)` — the non-vacuity precondition that stops the last conjunct passing on an empty set — carries no `wrong` key and is deliberately NOT counted, which is why the number is 4 and not 5; and a future conjunct that folds into an existing key would be invisible. Upgrade named in the comment: have the check return the conjunct names as a tuple.

resolutions.what: `tasks/reviews/pr58-r1-resolution.json` R1 gains a `correction` object. The original claim is left standing verbatim above it, per the orchestrator's constraint: the correction states that `docs/analysis.md` was already reachable by `analysis_section1` (since PR #44 R4) and `analysis_coverage`, both configured in the same case file, and gives the real reason `doc_quotes` was needed — `analysis_section1` formats against `vals` (`actions`/`with_browser`/`total`/`remaining`, all report-derived), so `{live}`/`{live_sites}` raise KeyError there.
resolutions.red_first: none possible — this is a claim in a review record about the state of the code, not a property of the tree. Verified by reading: `_run_doc_counts_case`'s `analysis_section1` block reads `(RUN_ROOT / s1['doc'])` and formats against `vals`, which has no suite-count key.
resolutions.found_while_checking: not part of the finding, recorded because it strengthens the conclusion: `analysis_section1` is also gated on a non-red headline report (`if s1 and (head := ...)`), so a suite count parked in that hook would stop being graded exactly when the cited report goes red — which is when prose is most likely to be stale. That is a second reason `doc_quotes` is the right hook, and it makes R8's alternative acceptance (fold into the existing hook) the worse of the two options offered.
